html:
A poet, scholar and teacher of the Sokoto Caliphate in what is now northern Nigeria. She was a daughter of Usman dan Fodio, the founder of the caliphate, and a sister of its second ruler, Muhammad Bello.

She knew the Quran by heart and wrote more than sixty works in Arabic, Fulfulde and Hausa, in poems about history, law, medicine, and the lives of holy women. Her poems also recorded the wars of the jihad.

Her most lasting work was a network of women teachers called the 'yan taru, "those who gather together". She trained them, and they travelled to villages to teach rural women, using her poems as lessons. She is often held up today as a model of Muslim women's education in West Africa, and schools and centres in Nigeria bear her name.
